# pve_sdn_fabric_ospf (Resource)

Manages an OSPF SDN fabric (`/cluster/sdn/fabrics/fabric`, section protocol `ospf`) with its per-node member entries (`/cluster/sdn/fabrics/node/{fabric_id}`). Changes stay pending and take effect only after the `pve_sdn_apply` action runs. The pin marks `ip_prefix` and `ip6_prefix` as not deletable on OSPF fabrics: clearing them in configuration leaves the upstream value in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# OSPF SDN fabric with one node member. Changes stay pending until the
# `pve_sdn_apply` action pushes them cluster-wide.
resource "pve_sdn_fabric_ospf" "ospf1" {
  fabric_id = "ospf1"
  ip_prefix = "10.0.0.0/24"
  area      = "0.0.0.0"

  redistribute = [
    {
      source    = "connected"
      route_map = null
    },
  ]

  nodes = [
    {
      node_id = "pve1"
      ip      = "10.0.0.1"
      ip6     = null
      interfaces = [
        {
          name         = "ens19"
          ip           = "10.0.0.1/24"
          ip6          = null
          network_type = "point-to-point"
        },
      ]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `fabric_id` (String) The fabric identifier (PVE `pve-sdn-fabric-id`: 2 - 8 characters of letters, digits, or hyphens, starting and ending alphanumeric). Changing this value forces recreation.

### Optional

- `area` (String) OSPF area, either an IPv4 address or a 32-bit number (e.g. `0.0.0.0`).
- `ip6_prefix` (String) IPv6 prefix (CIDR) node addresses are drawn from, e.g. `fd00::/64`.
- `ip_prefix` (String) IPv4 prefix (CIDR) node addresses are drawn from, e.g. `10.0.0.0/24`.
- `nodes` (Attributes List) Per-node member entries of the fabric. Each entry joins the named cluster node into the OSPF fabric. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))
- `redistribute` (Attributes List) Route sources redistributed into OSPF, each with an optional route map filter. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--redistribute))
- `route_filter` (String) Prefix list (see `pve_sdn_prefix_list`) used to filter routes installed into the kernel routing table.

### Read-Only

- `digest` (String) Configuration digest of the fabric; changes whenever the fabric configuration changes.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Required:

- `node_id` (String) The cluster node name.

Optional:

- `interfaces` (Attributes List) Network interfaces participating in OSPF on this node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--interfaces))
- `ip` (String) IPv4 address of this node inside the fabric.
- `ip6` (String) IPv6 address of this node inside the fabric.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.interfaces`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the network interface (e.g. `ens19`).

Optional:

- `ip` (String) IPv4 address (CIDRv4) for this interface, e.g. `10.0.0.1/24`.
- `ip6` (String) IPv6 address (CIDRv6) for this interface.
- `network_type` (String) OSPF network type of the interface. Must be one of: `broadcast`, `non-broadcast`, `point-to-multipoint`, `point-to-point`.



<a id="nestedatt--redistribute"></a>
### Nested Schema for `redistribute`

Required:

- `source` (String) The protocol to redistribute routes from. Must be one of: `bgp`, `connected`, `kernel`, `static`.

Optional:

- `route_map` (String) Route map (see `pve_sdn_route_map`) filtering or transforming routes redistributed from this source.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing OSPF fabric by its identifier:
terraform import pve_sdn_fabric_ospf.ospf1 ospf1
```
